name: MI-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Detroit-based district with a D+22 partisan lean makes the Democratic nominee a heavy favorite
Donavan McKinney enters the general after defeating Rep. Shri Thanedar in the primary, with about $1.8 million raised and outside support on both sides
Republican nominee T. P. Nykoriak shows no reported fundraising, cash on hand, or outside spending
Prediction markets price a Democratic win around 98%, with no public polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The seat's deep Democratic lean plus the nominee's clear financial edge leave the general election largely a formality; the real contest was settled when McKinney unseated Thanedar in the primary.
model.watch: A surge from the independent or minor-party candidates, or damaging news about McKinney, could narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Shri Thanedar (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Michigan's 13th District, anchored in Detroit, is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 22 points toward Democrats. Shri Thanedar's primary loss to Donavan McKinney settled the real contest; the general election now features McKinney against Republican T. P. Nykoriak and several minor-party or independent candidates.

McKinney has raised about $1.8 million and drawn both supporting and opposing outside spending, while the Republican nominee reports no fundraising or cash on hand. No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets put the Democratic side's chances near 98%. With such a large structural advantage and little evidence of competitive opposition, the seat remains safely Democratic, and the main question is the size of the margin rather than the winner.
